title: T and N and the space bar
summary: The two keys with bumps, the space bar, and the habit of not looking down.
intro: The keys with a small bump are where everything starts. Both index fingers rest there and do not wander; the rest of the course is measured from that position. Start by placing both hands and looking only at the screen.
congrats: Your hands are in place. From here on, everything is a key you reach from this position and let go of again.

screens.text: This key belongs to your left index finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only T and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
t t tt
tttt
tttttt tttttt

screens.text: This key belongs to your right index finger. Find it without looking, press it once, and let the finger return. The way back matters as much as the press.
Only N and what you already know. Slowly, and bring the finger back to the home row after every press.
screens.content:
nt nt
nt tn ntnt
tn nt tntn

screens.text: The space bar belongs to your right thumb. The thumbs do nothing else, which is why you never have to look for it.
screens.hint: Press the space bar to continue

screens.text: Short groups with spaces between them. The right thumb goes down and up; every other finger stays put.
screens.content:
nt nt
tn nt tntn
nnnn tttt

screens.text: Short groups, one after another. Keep going to the end even if you miss one.
The new keys mixed with the old ones, which is how they will turn up inside words.
screens.content:
tn tn
tn nt tntn
tttt nnnn

screens.text: The two new keys once more. There are no words to write with them yet, and that is expected.
screens.content:
tn nt

nt tn ntnt

screens.text: Slightly longer groups. Hurrying does not help yet.
Everything you have so far, in short groups. Eyes on the screen, not on your hands.

screens.text: Back to patterns for a moment, to check that the fingers still find their way home.
